findings.claim: `self.downsize` is defined twice in OptimizedImage. Ruby has no overloading, so the later (from, to, dimensions, opts) definition replaces the (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) one, and existing 5-argument callers such as ResizeEmoji (app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14) raise ArgumentError.

verifier.reason: app/models/optimized_image.rb:145 and :149 both define `self.downsize`; the later `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` definition replaces the first and accepts at most 4 arguments, so the 5-argument call at app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 (`downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`) raises ArgumentError.

findings.claim: API URL-based uploads now call FileHelper.download with a hardcoded 10.megabytes cap instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. This ignores the configured limit: larger files are truncated or blocked on sites allowing more than 10 MB, and more than allowed is downloaded on sites with smaller limits.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 now passes a hardcoded `10.megabytes` to `FileHelper.download` where it used `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, and lib/file_helper.rb:18 stops writing once that cap is passed, so URL uploads are truncated at about 10 MB on sites configured higher and up to 10 MB is fetched on sites configured lower. The lower-limit case is softened because images are downsized afterwards (uploads_controller.rb:64-69) and lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:81-85 still enforces the configured size before storing.

findings.claim: Client-side upload validation hardcodes maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 for all upload types instead of using Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']. Files the server will reject can pass the browser check, and files that sites configured above 10 MB allow are blocked.

verifier.reason: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 now sets `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` for every `type` (and again at :246 for the 413 message), replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. The server-side downsizing added at app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-66 only covers images, so attachments between `max_attachment_size_kb` (default 3072, config/site_settings.yml:516-518) and 10 MB pass the browser check, and sites configured above 10 MB are blocked client-side.

findings.claim: The same 10 MB constant is duplicated in several places, so the client and server limits can drift apart.

verifier.reason: The patch hardcodes 10 MB as separate literals in three places: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 and :246 (`10 * 1024`) and app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 (`10.megabytes`). They replace the SiteSetting lookups and have no shared source, so client and server values can drift independently.

findings.claim: The HTTP 413 handler always reports a limit of 10240 KB, although the actual limit depends on the nginx/proxy client_max_body_size setting.

verifier.reason: The 413 branch at app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:245-248 hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` and shows it in the `file_too_large` message. A 413 comes from the web server, whose limit is set separately (config/nginx.sample.conf:61 `client_max_body_size 10m` is only a sample; docs/INSTALL-ubuntu.md:390 mentions 2m), so the reported figure can be wrong.

findings.claim: The error message in displayErrorForUpload (line 246) shows a hardcoded 10 MB instead of the actual configured limit when the server rejects a file for exceeding a smaller configured limit.

verifier.reason: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 sets `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` in the 413 branch, replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`, so a 413 from a web server configured below 10 MB (which config/nginx.sample.conf:60-61 says to keep in sync with the site setting) reports "maximum size is 10240kb". Rejections by the app's own size validator are unaffected (lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:85 sends the configured limit via `data.errors`), so only the 413 path is wrong.

findings.claim: In the switch statement, `case 413` declares `maxSizeKB` without a surrounding block, so the declaration is visible to the other cases.

verifier.reason: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:245-246 has `case 413:` followed directly by `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024;` with no braces, so the declaration is visible to `case 422` and the rest of the function. It is harmless in practice: `var` is function-scoped anyway, no other case uses the name, and the unbraced declaration existed before the patch, which only changed the initializer.

findings.claim: The downsize loop reads `tempfile.size`, which stays stale after the in-place downsize and ImageOptim rename. As a result, the loop may run all passes or fail to terminate correctly, and Upload.create_for receives a stale filesize, dimensions and a mismatched sha1.

verifier.reason: The loop condition and the `Upload.create_for` argument both read `tempfile.size` on the open Tempfile (app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66,72), while each pass ends in `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)` (app/models/optimized_image.rb:164), which replaces the path by rename, so the handle keeps reporting the old size; the loop can burn all 5 attempts, the stale filesize is then checked by lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:84, and `FastImage.new(file)` (app/models/upload.rb:71) reads stale dimensions. The rename is image_optim 0.20.2 gem behaviour recalled from memory, not read here, and the sha1 part is overstated: `Digest::SHA1.file(file)` (upload.rb:106) reopens by path, so it matches the stored file.

findings.claim: Downsizing passes '80%' as the dimensions. For animated GIFs this goes to `gifsicle --resize-fit`, which accepts only WxH pixel geometry, so gifsicle fails and every retry attempt is used up.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 passes "80%" with allow_animation (default true), and for a path ending in .gif app/models/optimized_image.rb:155 and :137-138 route it to `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%` (:120), which takes only WxH geometry; convert_with returns false (:162) and the loop at uploads_controller.rb:66-69 spends all 5 attempts on an unchanged file. Reachable at least for API URL uploads, where lib/file_helper.rb:13-14 keeps the .gif extension on the tempfile; browser multipart uploads under the locked rack 1.5.5 probably get an extensionless tempfile and skip this branch, and gifsicle's rejection of "80%" rests on its documented behaviour, not on a run here.

findings.claim: The allow_animation option is effectively dead code, because animated GIF downsizing fails through both upload paths.

verifier.reason: The new call at app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 cannot produce a downsized animated GIF on either path: multipart tempfiles have no `.gif` extension under the pinned rack 1.5.5, so the check at app/models/optimized_image.rb:155 never selects the animated branch and `convert from[0]` keeps only the first frame; URL downloads keep the extension (lib/file_helper.rb:13-14) but then run `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%` (optimized_image.rb:120,137-138), which gifsicle rejects because it wants WxH. The rack and gifsicle behaviour is from my knowledge of those tools, not from code in this repo.

findings.claim: Each upload can trigger up to 5 sequential ImageMagick plus ImageOptim runs on files up to 10 MB.

verifier.reason: The patch adds a loop at app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65-69 that calls OptimizedImage.downsize up to 5 times while the image exceeds max_image_size_kb; each call shells out to `convert` (gifsicle for animated GIFs) and then runs ImageOptim.new.optimize_image! in convert_with (app/models/optimized_image.rb:160-164). The 10 MB bound comes from the URL download cap at uploads_controller.rb:55, the client check in utilities.js and nginx client_max_body_size 10m (config/nginx.sample.conf:61).

findings.claim: When OptimizedImage.downsize fails and returns false, the loop ignores the result, keeps retrying, and lets the oversized file continue.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66-69 discards the return value of OptimizedImage.downsize (which returns false on failure, app/models/optimized_image.rb:160-169), so a failing convert is re-run up to 5 times and the still-oversized tempfile is passed to Upload.create_for at line 72. The file is not actually stored, though: lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:80-87 rejects it with a too-large error, so the cost is wasted work and no early exit.

findings.claim: The downsize loop shrinks the image to only about 33% of the original after 5 iterations (0.8^5), so an image can still exceed max_image_size_kb and proceed to Upload.create_for.

verifier.reason: The loop at app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65-69 stops after 5 passes at 80% with no size check afterwards, so a still-oversized image does reach Upload.create_for at line 72. It is not stored, though: Validators::UploadValidator#maximum_file_size (lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:80-87) rejects it at upload.save (app/models/upload.rb:135) with a too_large error, so the only effect is a late rejection.

findings.claim: Non-API uploads run in the shared Scheduler::Defer.later queue, so large uploads stall unrelated deferred work.

verifier.reason: Non-API (non-synchronous) uploads run `create_upload` inside `Scheduler::Defer.later("Create Upload")` at app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:19-22, and that queue is drained serially by a single worker thread (lib/scheduler/defer.rb:55-58, 64-68). The patch adds up to five blocking ImageMagick downsize shell-outs to that deferred block (uploads_controller.rb:64-70) and raises the client-side limit to 10MB, so other deferred jobs wait behind large image uploads.

findings.claim: No tests cover the new downsize loop, the changed OptimizedImage.downsize/optimize signatures, or the client validation change.

verifier.reason: The patch touches only utilities.js, uploads_controller.rb and optimized_image.rb and adds no tests; nothing under spec/ references `downsize` or `OptimizedImage.optimize`, and spec/controllers/uploads_controller_spec.rb has no case for an image over `max_image_size_kb`. The one existing client test (test/javascripts/lib/utilities-test.js.es6:52-61) still asserts the old `max_image_size_kb = 5` limit and was not updated, so it contradicts the new hardcoded 10MB check at utilities.js:182 instead of covering it.

findings.claim: Image processing uses the same path for input and output, so the original file is lost if the operation fails mid-write.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, so `convert`/`gifsicle` (app/models/optimized_image.rb:126-134, 160-162) overwrite the only server-side copy of the upload in place. The return value is ignored, so a failed or partial write leaves a damaged tempfile that still goes to `Upload.create_for` at line 72.

findings.claim: With allow_animated_thumbnails off, `convert file[0]` writes only the first frame back over the original GIF.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 calls OptimizedImage.downsize with the tempfile path as both source and destination; with allow_animation false, optimize (app/models/optimized_image.rb:153-157) picks downsize_instructions (126-134), which runs `convert #{from}[0] ... #{to}` and so overwrites the uploaded GIF with its first frame only. This only triggers when the upload exceeds max_image_size_kb, and the setting defaults to true (config/site_settings.yml:574).

findings.claim: For regular browser uploads, Rack tempfile paths lack a .gif extension, so the GIF detection regex in optimize() never matches and `convert` with [0] strips animation from GIFs.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:58,67 passes `file.tempfile.path` to `OptimizedImage.downsize`, and app/models/optimized_image.rb:155 only picks the animated (gifsicle) path when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`; otherwise it runs `convert #{from}[0]` (optimized_image.rb:129), keeping only the first frame. Gemfile.lock:231 pins rack 1.5.5, whose multipart parser (not vendored here, recalled from Rack source) creates `Tempfile.new("RackMultipart")` with no extension, so oversized animated GIFs uploaded from a browser are flattened.

findings.claim: The `tempfile &&` and `tempfile.size > 0` checks in the new guard are redundant with the loop condition and the later handling of a nil tempfile.

verifier.reason: In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 the `tempfile.size > 0` check is subsumed by the loop condition at :66 (`tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, with the setting already required to be > 0). The `tempfile &&` check changes nothing observable because a nil tempfile raises NoMethodError at :72 (`tempfile.size`) anyway — though that is a crash, not real nil handling; only the `ensure` at :85 tolerates nil.

findings.claim: FileHelper.is_image? matches .svg, so oversized SVGs enter the downsize loop and ImageMagick rewrites the user's SVG in place.

verifier.reason: `FileHelper.images` includes "svg" (lib/file_helper.rb:31), and the new loop at app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-69 is gated only on `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`, so an oversized SVG is passed to `convert <path>[0] -resize 80% <same path>` (app/models/optimized_image.rb:126-134) with no SVG guard, unlike the special-casing at app/models/optimized_image.rb:45 and app/models/upload.rb:63. What ImageMagick actually writes back was not run here; it depends on the installed delegates.

findings.claim: An inline `rescue nil` silently swallows all exceptions, including network errors.

verifier.reason: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 reads `tempfile = FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...) rescue nil`, which discards any StandardError (network/HTTP/timeout errors included) and leaves `tempfile` nil, so line 72's `tempfile.size` then fails with an unrelated NoMethodError. The `rescue nil` was already on this line before the patch, which only changed the size argument.
